parameters.name: overrepresentation_analysis
parameters.label: Enable overrepresented analysis
parameters.help: Enable overrepresented sequence analysis.

parameters.name: overrepresentation_sampling
parameters.label: Overrepresentation sampling
parameters.help: One in (--overrepresentation_sampling) reads will be computed for overrepresentation analysis (1~10000), smaller is slower, default is 20.

parameters.name: disable_quality_filtering
parameters.label: Disable quality filtering
parameters.help: Quality filtering is enabled by default. If this option is specified, quality filtering is disabled.

parameters.name: qualified_quality_phred
parameters.label: Qualified quality phred
parameters.help: The quality value that a base is qualified. Default 15 means phred quality >=Q15 is qualified.

parameters.name: unqualified_percent_limit
parameters.label: Unqualified percent limit
parameters.help: How many percents of bases are allowed to be unqualified (0~100). Default 40 means 40%.

parameters.name: n_base_limit
parameters.label: N base limit
parameters.help: If one read's number of N base is >n_base_limit, then this read/pair is discarded. Default is 5.

parameters.name: disable_length_filtering
parameters.label: Disable length filtering
parameters.help: Length filtering is enabled by default. If this option is specified, length filtering is disabled.

parameters.name: length_required
parameters.label: Length required
parameters.help: Reads shorter than this value will be discarded. Default is 15.

parameters.name: length_limit
parameters.label: Maximum length
parameters.help: Reads longer than this value will be discarded. Default is 0 and means no limitation.

parameters.name: enable_low_complexity_filter
parameters.label: Enable low complexity filter
parameters.help: The complexity is defined as the percentage of base that is different from its next base, default is No

parameters.name: complexity_threshold
parameters.label: Complexity threshold
parameters.help: Threshold for low complexity filter (0~100). Default is 30, which means 30% complexity is required.

test_parameter.name: eval_dups
test_parameter.label: Enable duplicated reads analysis
test_parameter.help: If enabled, calculate and report read duplication statistics. Enabling this is also a prerequisite for optional deduplication of reads. Duplicate detection relies exclusively on exact identity between read sequences (both for SE and PE data). It also increases tool memory requirements and running time moderately. NOTE: the default (no duplication analysis) is different from the command-line tool.

test_parameter.name: trimming_select
test_parameter.label: PolyG tail trimming
test_parameter.help: This feature is enabled for NextSeq/NovaSeq data by default. NextSeq/NovaSeq data is detected by the machine ID in the FASTQ records.

options.label: Automatic trimming for Illumina NextSeq/NovaSeq data

parameters.name: poly_g_min_len
parameters.label: PolyG minimum length
parameters.help: The minimum length to detect polyG in the read tail. 10 by default.

parameters.name: poly_g_min_len
parameters.label: PolyG minimum length
parameters.help: The minimum length to detect polyG in the read tail. 10 by default.

test_parameter.name: polyx_trimming_select
test_parameter.label: PolyX tail trimming
test_parameter.help: Similar to polyG tail trimming. When polyG tail trimming and polyX tail trimming are both enabled, fastp will perform polyG trimming first, then perform polyX trimming. Disabled by default.

parameters.name: poly_x_min_len
parameters.label: PolyX minimum length
parameters.help: The minimum length to detect polyX in the read tail. 10 by default.

parameters.name: umi
parameters.label: Enable unique molecular identifer
parameters.help: Enable unique molecular identifer (UMI) preprocessing.

parameters.name: umi_loc
parameters.label: UMI location
parameters.help: Specify the location of UMI, can be (index1/index2/read1/read2/per_index/per_read, default is none.

parameters.name: umi_len
parameters.label: UMI length
parameters.help: If the UMI is in read1/read2, its length should be provided.

parameters.name: umi_prefix
parameters.label: UMI prefix
parameters.help: If specified, an underline will be used to connect prefix and UMI (i.e. prefix=UMI, UMI=AATTCG, final=UMI_AATTCG). No prefix by default.

test_parameter.name: cut_front
test_parameter.label: Cut by quality in front (5')
test_parameter.help: Enable per read cutting by quality in front (5'). (WARNING: this will interfere with deduplication of both PE/SE data if performed with downstream tools.)

parameters.name: cut_front_window_size
parameters.label: Cutting window size for cut front
parameters.help: The size of the sliding window for sliding window trimming.

parameters.name: cut_front_mean_quality
parameters.label: Cutting mean quality for cut front
parameters.help: The bases in the sliding window with mean quality below cutting_quality will be cut.

test_parameter.name: cut_tail
test_parameter.label: Cut by quality in tail (3')
test_parameter.help: Enable per read cutting by quality in tail (3'). (WARNING: this will interfere with deduplication of SE data if performed with downstream tools.)

parameters.name: cut_tail_window_size
parameters.label: Cutting window size for cut tail
parameters.help: The size of the sliding window for sliding window trimming.

parameters.name: cut_tail_mean_quality
parameters.label: Cutting mean quality for cut tail
parameters.help: The bases in the sliding window with mean quality below cutting_quality will be cut.

test_parameter.name: cut_right
test_parameter.label: Cut by quality in tail (3')
test_parameter.help: Move a sliding window from front to tail, if meet one window with mean quality < threshold, drop the bases in the window and the right part, and then stop. (WARNING: this will interfere with deduplication of SE data if performed with downstream tools.)

parameters.name: cut_right_window_size
parameters.label: Cutting window size for cut right
parameters.help: The size of the sliding window for sliding window trimming.

parameters.name: cut_right_mean_quality
parameters.label: Cutting mean quality for cut right
parameters.help: The bases in the sliding window with mean quality below cutting_quality will be cut.

parameters.name: correction
parameters.label: Enable base correction
parameters.help: Enable base correction in overlapped regions (only for PE data), default is disabled.

parameters.name: report_html
parameters.label: Output HTML report
parameters.help: fastp provides a QC report for the data Before and After filtering within a single HTML page, which enables comparison of the quality statistics changed by the preprocessing step directly

parameters.name: report_json
parameters.label: Output JSON report
parameters.help: The JSON report contains all the data visualized in the HTML report. The format of the JSON report is manually optimized to be easily readable by humans and is compatible with MultiQC

help.content:
.. class:: infomark

**What it does**

fastp_ is a tool designed to provide fast all-in-one preprocessing for FASTQ files. This tool is developed in C++ with multithreading supported to
afford high performance.

*Features*

1. Filter out bad (too low quality, too short, or too many N...) and/or duplicate reads

2. Cut low quality bases for per read in its 5' and 3' by evaluating the mean quality from a sliding window (like Trimmomatic but faster)

3. Trim all reads in front and tail

4. Cut adapters. Adapter sequences can be automatically detected, which means you don't have to input the adapter sequences to trim them.

5. Correct mismatched base pairs in overlapped regions of paired end reads, if one base is with high quality while the other is with ultra-low quality

6. Trim polyG in 3' ends, which is commonly seen in NovaSeq/NextSeq data. Trim polyX in 3' ends to remove unwanted polyX tailing (i.e. polyA tailing for mRNA-Seq data)

7. Preprocess unique molecular identifier (UMI) enabled data, shift UMI to sequence name

8. Report JSON format result for further interpreting

9. Visualize quality control and filtering results on a single HTML page (like FASTQC but faster and more informative)

10. Split the output to multiple files (0001.R1.gz, 0002.R1.gz...) to support parallel processing. Two modes can be used, limiting the total split file number, or limiting the lines of each split file (*Not enabled in this Galaxy tool*)

11. Support long reads (data from PacBio / Nanopore devices)

-----

**Inputs**

Single-end or Paired-end (compressed) fastqsanger files

-----

**Outputs**

    * Processed reads
    * Merged reads
    * Unmerged filtered reads, reads that cannot be merged successfully, but both pass all the filters.
    * Unmerged unfiltered reads, reads that cannot be merged, i.e. **forward** passes filters but **reverse** doesn't.

Optionally, under **Output Options** you can choose to output

    * HTML report (default is Yes)
    * JSON report (compatible with MultiQC)

.. _fastp: https://github.com/OpenGene/fastp
